paras: I'm Mollie Allison and I am currently studying for my Postgraduate Diploma in Clinical Exercise Physiology. I am based in Hamilton, and in my spare time I coach volleyball and beach volleyball to all ages, from 5-year-olds to adults.

I currently represent New Zealand in beach volleyball as part of the NZA squad, as well as playing competitive indoor volleyball during the winter. I love spending all my time on the courts, training hard myself but also giving back and teaching all I know to those around me.
A big pro of playing beach volleyball is being able to train outdoors and at beaches. A big con is not having many people to train with in my area, as well as everything being largely self-funded.
My biggest achievements to date would be representing NZ in America and Australia, and consistently making the top 5 on the New Zealand Beach Tour at a young age.
My ultimate goal is to be part of New Zealand's top partnership and represent all over the world.
X-ZONE will help me with my performance and to achieve my goals by managing muscle soreness, warming up effectively, recovering better and staying consistent through high-intensity training.

ig.headline: Top five on the NZ Beach Tour
ig.subline: Ambassador 14: Mollie Allison, NZ beach volleyball
ig.quote: I love spending all my time on the courts, training hard myself but also giving back and teaching all I know to those around me.
ig.caption:
Consistency is what turns training into results.

Mollie Allison represents New Zealand in beach volleyball and has played for NZ in America and Australia. She has made the top five on the New Zealand Beach Tour again and again, at a young age.

She does it from Hamilton, a long way from the nearest beach court, with few training partners and largely self-funded. In between, she is studying clinical exercise physiology and coaching everyone from 5-year-olds to adults.

Her goal: to be part of New Zealand's top partnership and play all over the world.

For Mollie, X-ZONE is part of staying consistent: managing muscle soreness, warming up and recovering through high-intensity training.

Read Mollie's full story, link in bio.
